subject: Request: Priority GPU Allocation for Sapphire Systems (Q3 onboarding)
messages:
From: Holly Mason <holly@sapphire.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@sapphire.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority allocation request — Sapphire Q3 onboarding

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. We are targeting a guarded public launch of our new assistant in mid-September and the success metric baseline requires consistently low L99 latency for peak traffic (we estimate 2.2M inference tokens/day at launch). As discussed, we would like to request priority access to a dedicated GPU tranche for Q3 so we can complete the validation and warm the model caches.

Attached is a conservative capacity request (Sapphire_Capacity_Request_Q3.xlsx) that shows expected peak windows by PST and the burst profile for the first 8 weeks. Our commercial is near-final; we plan to sign the reserved capacity contract by 7/9 if we can secure a clear capacity path.

Main asks:
- A provisional allocation of 8 A100-equivalent slots (or equivalent compute profile) with a 4-week warm-up buffer prior to launch.
- Confirmation of fallback tiers/policy and whether preemptible burst is acceptable as part of the plan.
- Timeline for a hard commitment (what info/legal/PO you need by 7/9).

We appreciate any guidance on tradeoffs (latency vs cost) and whether a staged onboarding (canary weight) is preferable to a full allocation at day 1. Aaron and I are available for a quick call tomorrow morning.

Best,
Holly Mason
Head of Product, Sapphire Systems
holly@sapphire.ai

--

Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority allocation request — Sapphire Q3 onboarding

Holly — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. I’ve looped in Markus (runtime) and Monica (sales ops) to size this and run the allocation process. High level: we want to avoid overcommit risk while giving you the predictability you need.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Markus to confirm feasible capacity footprint (A100-equivalent) and whether 8 slots is the right baseline for your token profile.
2) Monica to propose contract/term template and confirm what counts as the hard commitment we need by 7/9 (PO, signed SOW, payment terms).
3) Outline a fallback plan (preemptible burst + canary ramp) and caveats for SLA during warm-up.

We will aim to give a provisional decision by EOD Wed (6/23). If anything is urgent, happy to jump on a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, Holly Mason <holly@sapphire.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority allocation request — Sapphire Q3 onboarding

Holly, Nikhil — I reviewed the attached sheet and ran a quick capacity estimate. A few notes: 

- The 2.2M tokens/day baseline with peak windows concentrated in PST evening will create strong burst pressure across the fleet if we give a pure reserved slice without intelligent routing.
- 8 A100-equivalent slots looks reasonable for steady throughput, but you will need additional burst capacity (2–4 slots) for the first 6 weeks while caches and KV warming complete.

Operational options (pros/cons):
A) Reserved tranche (8 slots) + scheduled warm-up burst (2–4 slots) for first 6 weeks. Pros: predictable latency; Cons: higher cost if reserved at full capacity.
B) Reserved tranche (6 slots) + preemptible burst for peak windows. Pros: lower committed cost; Cons: potential increased latency risk during rare preemption events.
C) Staged canary: start with 25% traffic on reserved tranche + burst to validate, scale to 100% over 3 weeks. Pros: safer roll; Cons: longer time to full capacity.

Technically, we can implement a mixed policy: A at launch with automatic fallback to B (preemptible) if queue depth crosses threshold. That requires a runbook and a short SLA exception for the warm-up period. I uploaded a sketch of the runbook (capacity-options-runbook.md) for review.

If you want a guaranteed hard slice for launch, we need signed commitment by 7/2 (earlier than your 7/9 ask) to lock slots in the Q3 tranche. Without that we can still prioritize but not guarantee hard isolation during a concurrent producer surge.

I’ll be available for a tech call Wed 6/23 at 9:00am PT to walk through the runbook and scheduling.

—Markus Klein
Senior Director, Serving Runtime
markus@redwood.com

--
Attachment: capacity-options-runbook.md (text, 6 sections)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Holly Mason <holly@sapphire.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority allocation request — Sapphire Q3 onboarding

Holly — quick commercial note from our side: to reserve an 8-slot tranche with the warm-up burst plan Markus suggested, the commercial terms we recommend are:

- 6-month committed reserved tranche (monthly billing) with a 30% discount off on-demand units.
- A one-time warm-up credit applied if you hit the validation milestones (canary pass, integration smoke tests) within the first 30 days.
- If you accept staged canary instead of immediate full tranche, we would reduce the reserved commitment to 4–6 slots for month 1 with an automated step-up to 8 based on traffic thresholds.

What we need from you to lock the tranche by 7/2: signed SOW + PO or payment details + agreement on warm-up milestones (I can send a SOW template by EOD). If your procurement timeline truly needs until 7/9 we can hold this as a high-priority pending allocation but cannot guarantee hard isolation beyond provisional prioritization.

If it helps, I can draft two contract options (Immediate Reserve vs Staged Canary) and share redlined templates.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_terms_v2.pdf (PDF, 9 pages)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority allocation request — Sapphire Q3 onboarding

Holly — following the tech and commercial checks above, here’s the provisional plan we will put in writing later today:

1) Provisional allocation: Redwood will prioritize Sapphire for a reserved tranche equivalent to 6 A100 slots with automated scheduled burst of +2 slots for the first 6 weeks (effectively supporting your 8-slot peak while you warm caches). This is a provisional prioritization with a conditional commit.
2) Hard isolation: To guarantee hard isolation and lock the Q3 tranche, we require signed SOW + PO by 2027-07-02. Monica will send both contract templates (Immediate Reserve and Staged Canary) so you can choose.
3) Fallback & SLA: During the 6-week warm-up we will accept an SLA exception that allows preemptible fallback during severe fleet pressure; we will provide a playbook and weekly validation checkpoints.
4) Next steps: Monica to send SOW and draft invoice; Markus to run the canary runbook on a staging window 6/23–6/30; Holly/Aaron to confirm which contract option you prefer by 6/30.

We’ll also open a short-term capacity hold in the scheduling queue (high-priority pending contract). This gives you priority placement but not guaranteed hard isolation until the paperwork is complete.

If that timeline works, please confirm and Monica will issue the next items. Happy to take a call this afternoon if you want to finalize.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com
